chunks: 22. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Bishr, from Muhammad ibn Jamhur al-Ami, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl ibn Yasar, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said regarding the Great Lordship and the Great Divinity: 'No thing comes to be from nothing except Allah, and no thing is transferred from its substance to another substance except Allah, and no thing is transferred from existence to non-existence except Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three exclusive acts of Allah mentioned in this hadith regarding creation and substance?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the doctrine of Divine Unity by identifying three specific acts exclusive to Allah: creation ex nihilo, substantial transformation, and the transition from existence to non-existence. It serves as a foundational argument against polytheism and anthropomorphism, affirming that all ontological changes are direct manifestations of God’s will rather than independent causal agents.
